description: The graph illustrates the training loss over time for two methods—Vanilla and SepLLM—during the training of a large language model. The x-axis represents the training time in seconds, ranging from 0 to 250,000, with major tick marks at intervals of 50,000. The y-axis shows the loss value, scaled linearly from 2.40 to 2.75, with major tick marks at 0.05 intervals. The Vanilla method is represented by a purple line with triangle markers, which starts at a loss of approximately 2.75 and steadily decreases to about 2.50 by the end of the training period. The SepLLM method is shown as a red line with circle markers, beginning at a similar loss of around 2.75 and decreasing more rapidly than Vanilla, reaching a loss of approximately 2.48 by the end. A green dashed horizontal line at a loss of 2.50 is drawn across the graph, and a green vertical dashed line at approximately 200,000 seconds marks a point where the SepLLM loss intersects this threshold. A green annotation indicates that at this point, the SepLLM method achieves a 1.26 times faster convergence compared to the Vanilla method, as it reaches the same loss level in less time.
